normal.name: schamspeare
normal.text: When I read that there are between six and eight new card sets a year, I just thought, how is this sustainable? But then I read that they also cycle as many older sets out. Okay, so it’s rigged both ways. The cards you bought are phased out, and there is a constant churn of new ones you have to buy to stay competitive. And with each new set, some new IP is introduced, watering down whatever was inherently Magic in Magic the Gathering. (7) #MTG #MTGArena #games

normal.name: schamspeare
normal.text: But that’s not most of us. Most of us find the obvious synergies, the ones that have been thought through and hardcoded into the game by the designers; or we copy what we see other players capitalizing on. If you’re in this latter group and you credit yourself with building a cool, powerful deck, that’s another illusion that you have fallen victim to. You’re one of tens of thousands who is reading the text and following the deck-building cues you’re given. (6) #MTG #MTGArena #games

normal.name: schamspeare
normal.text: There is one kind of player for whom this is the right and perfect game: people who DO love a spreadsheet and who have the brains, time, and money to come up with interesting, game-breaking synergies, buy what they need to implement them, and tear up the meta with them. normal.name: schamspeare
normal.text: If you build a deck and win a few games with it, that’s probably as good as it gets. After that, you either keep playing with the same cards and at the same W / L rate, or you invest in packs of cards so that you can gain access to better cards. But the progress you make will be incremental and illusory when compared to the length of the climb and the essential balance of the game. (2) #MTG #MTGArena #games
